sections.transcript: Last Friday night, a Kelowna couple found a surprise while clearing the attic of their heritage house. Alex and Rebecca Castillo found a paper wasp nest in the attic. The nest was built by stinging insects that chew on wood fiber, mix it with their saliva, and spew out a substance they use as a building material. But this was no ordinary wasp nest. It was bright red, blue, and yellow, looking more like a piñata or party balloon than a nest. To solve the mystery, the Castillos didn't have to look far. In another room of the attic, they found four dusty boxes of old superhero comic books, books, which the wasps had used as raw material. Most of the comics had been chewed to shreds, but several were still sealed in their original plastic packaging. The Castillos brought the unharmed items to a collector shop and were told that one, a rare 1952 Superman comic in mint condition, is worth $1,600. Resolve to continue working on their house, the Castillos are now deciding whether to keep the item or sell it on eBay. You will watch a two-minute video, then eight questions will appear. Choose the best way to answer each question.

sections.transcript: You will watch a discussion among three business associates, two women and one man. They work at a bookstore. The discussion takes place at the bookstore. This is Naomi. This is Tasha. This is Nathan. So the first item on the agenda is the storefront window. The two of you have some concerns? Yes, we've been concerned about the message we're sending. For six of the last eight weeks we've been featuring a romance title, but we carry many other genres of fiction. We also carry nonfiction. Not only that, but we had 50 copies of the same title in the window. I mean, if we want to feature romance, we should have 50 different titles, one copy of each. Otherwise it's psychological manipulation. Yes, but the publisher of Love Wins paid us for exclusive use of that window. That's why we displayed only that title. You've been using our window for advertising? Since when? Oh, I don't like that at all. No, I agree with Nathan. I mean, what's in our window should represent what's on our shelves? Alternatively, we should put all our best books in our window. Isn't it our ultimate goal to stay in business? By attracting new customers? I mean, sure, by increasing advertising on one title, we will increase the sales of that title. You need the advertising revenue. It's as simple as that. No, I don't think it is. I mean, if you are selling our storefront display to the highest bidder, I'm afraid that we're heading in a really bad direction. People will start thinking of us as the romance bookstore, and they won't think of us when they want to buy literary fiction or nonfiction. We'll start losing customers, and then, therefore, we are going to start losing revenue. Couldn't we say have three different bookshelf levels in the window? We could have one for literary fiction, one for genre fiction, and on the last one we could put on fiction. Why can't we do that? Because no one will pay to have one copy of a book in a window. Yeah, but that's my point. Our storefront window shouldn't be for sale. The people who come to this mall do a lot of window browsing, and we should be using it to draw them into the store by showing them what's inside. Would you be willing to try my idea for two months? Just to compare statistics, we could look at how many people come in, we could look at sales and so on, and then we can come back and revisit the issue. Keep in mind that we're competing with other bookstores. I mean, there are two others right here in this mall, and people expect the stock in the window to represent the stock in the store. But publishers pay so much money. Okay, let's try it for a couple of months and then we'll see.

sections.transcript: As video gaming rises in popularity, the debate about its benefits and risks rages on, reviled by some as a cause of poor grades and aggressive behavior in children, video gaming is now just as likely to be touted as a way to develop important skills and facilitate learning. 6. Psychologist Thomas Moro sees a link between lower grades and frequent, unrestricted recreational video gaming. In his study of 1,500 students ages 8 to 18, those who devoted less time to video gaming boasted consistently higher academic achievement. Moro is quick to add that these findings should be interpreted cautiously since academic underachievement and the inclination to play video games could both stem from an unknown cause. Moro applies similar reasoning to his previous research correlating video gaming and aggression. Moro can't say that one causes the other. Both might be attributable to a third factor. Thus, for Moro, it's too soon to say that video games pose a risk to children's thoughts and emotions. But he does note that 85% of video games include violence, and children tend to mimic what they see. 40 year old Mike Hornveldt is no child, but he's an avid gamer. A University of Toronto professor specializing in the history of Canadian education, Dr. Hornveldt believes video games teach people how to learn. Hornveldt says video games engage players in a problem-solving cycle, hypothesis, experimentation, and eventual deduction are involved as players try different different options in an effort to solve a challenging problem. Horvelt says he enjoys collaborative multiplayer games, especially entrepreneurial business startup and management simulations, and he insists that they've helped him develop skills such as teamwork, mediation, and self-assessment. Where Moro and Horvelt see eye to eye is the claim that video gaming can become habit-forming. Moro points out that the average North American student plays nearly 10,000 hours of video games by the time they graduate college. Even Hornveld admits that he himself has fallen prey to the lure of interactive technology. The former compulsive 25-hour-a-week gamer now observes a strict weekly limit. Four hours, weekends only. A similar ability to self-regulate would be hard to find among children morrow notes, arguing that it is mostly up to parents to curb or even stop their child's video game playing before it gets out of hand. Children's brains are highly plastic, says Moro, and excessive game playing at a young age could have lifelong impacts. He recommends that parents not let children under five play video games at all, and says a limit of two hours a week is enough for everyone else.

paragraphs: To whom it may concern,

My name is Janet White and I am a tenant at your residential rental property, Garden Plaza, at 257 Pine Street, Apartment 502. I am writing to bring your attention to an ongoing issue regarding a broken heater in my rental unit. Unfortunately, even after numerous complaints, the problem has yet to be solved. As you can imagine, I am feeling very frustrated by the whole ordeal.

To recap, the heater in the living room of my apartment is broken. The average temperature in this room is between 15-17°C during the day and even lower at night. This is unacceptable as the local bylaw states that the landlord must keep the heat in rental apartments at a minimum of 20°C from October to April. I often work from home and find it hard to accomplish anything when I am freezing cold. I have had to purchase a small electric heater to keep myself warm which costs me money on my electricity bill. This is unfair because heat is supposed to be included in the rent I pay. In addition to my frustration with insufficient heat, there has been a lack of communication on your end about what has been done to solve the issue. The superintendent has never contacted me to let me know whether anyone has come to check out the heater. I had to call the head office on Tuesday, January 3rd, to find if there had been any attempt to rectify the problem. I was upset to find out that nothing had been done, even after submitting three complaint forms and leaving multiple voicemail messages about the issue.

At this point I am extremely disgruntled with the situation and the poor service I have received from your company. It has been over 3 weeks that I've been trying to deal with this problem. I feel that the manner in which this issue is being handled is completely unacceptable. I would like this situation to be resolved as soon as possible. I would also like to be contacted by your manager or supervisor at Johnson Realty Management to discuss what can be done to make up for the time, money, and frustration this issue has caused me.
Sincerely,
Janet White

paragraphs: A. Despite the increasing prevalence of purchasing and banking through electronic means, Canadian banknotes-commonly referred to as "carrying cash"-remain an important part of Canadian society. However, with the convenience of carrying cash also comes the risk of counterfeiting, or producing imitation currency without authorization from the government. Counterfeiting accounts for millions of dollars of losses to Canadian businesses and individuals each year. To combat this problem, the Bank of Canada introduced new polymer bills in 2013. These durable new bills are considered to be some of the most secure banknotes in the world.

B. The new series of polymer notes is designed in a way which is meant to portray the Canadian spirit of innovation and to celebrate Canada's national and international achievements. Each bill depicts a different innovation or event that has been a crucial aspect of Canadian history. The five-dollar bill, for example, illustrates the Canadarm2-an important contribution made to the International Space Station in April, 2001. The twenty-dollar bill depicts the Canadian National Vimy Memorial in honour of the sacrifices made by Canadians during the First World War. The one-hundred-dollar bill shows an insulin bottle to commemorate the 1922 discovery of insulin as a treatment for diabetes by Canadian researchers.

C. In addition to visually representing Canada, the new polymer bills are also designed to be more functional and environmentally friendly. The bills are able to withstand temperatures ranging from -75 to 140 degrees Celsius, are harder to tear, and do not absorb moisture, thereby allowing them to be wiped clean with a damp cloth. These improvements mean that, when properly handled, the new bills last up to 2.5 times longer than their paper predecessors. This increased lifespan and ability to be recycled means that polymer notes accomplish the important goal of reducing environmental impact.

D. Most importantly, the new polymer bills include a wide range of security features that are easy to verify and difficult to counterfeit. These features include raised ink located in various places on the surface of the bill, visual details such as transparent text and metallic features, and hidden numbers that can only be detected using an incandescent light. However, in spite of these innovative features, the best security against counterfeiting is still education. This is why front-line employees in Canadian businesses are taught to be both diligent and cautious when dealing in cash transactions.
E. Not given in any of the above paragraphs.

left.intro: Read the following article from a website.
paragraphs: In our digitally mediated age, many people seeking direct communion with fellow human beings have joined outdoor running groups, yours truly among them. Interestingly, it seems that the type of running terrain has an impact on fostering genuine human fellowship, among other benefits.

The Canadian Association of Sports and Movement claims the choice of terrain, be it dirt trail or hard pavement, is immaterial. But sports trainer David Rogers points out that hip and knee joints that routinely pound on dirt trails sustain less compression and, therefore, fewer injuries than those routinely subjected to unyielding asphalt. Granted, habitual pavement pounders may, on their first mountain trail runs, be humbled by the agility and concentration required to navigate around rocks and tree roots. Trail running has its challenges, but it is a healthier pursuit than road running. Away from urban automobile exhaust, a trail's lush greenery, stunning scenery, and boosted oxygen levels are exhilarating and psychologically restorative. I'm partial to what's known as the biophilia hypothesis: the desire to affiliate with nature is innate.

I think we need to tell that to search and rescue coordinator Simon Erholz, who is on public record as wishing more runners had an affinity for pavement. Erholz has publicly castigated the many novice trail runners who've fallen or lost their way and called for rescue. In this regard, it's understandable why so many marathoners opt to train on asphalt. "It's not that I don't want to admire Mother Nature while I'm running; I just want to put in my daily 10 kilometres with minimal chance of a face plant," says marathoner Nita Gill. "Also, running near my downtown condo gives me a sense I'm being monitored in a good way."

Memo to Nita: Safety, like beauty, is in the eye of the beholder. If you fall in a road race, participants will hop over you, single-mindedly fixated on the finish line. But in a trail race, they'll stop and carry you to the nearest first aid station. To me, if that's not soul-restoring communion with humanity, I don't know what is.

I am Ken Hoang who has borrowed 6000 dollars two months ago and I am currently repaying 600 dollars each month on a one-year contract. The money was very important and helpful for me because I have spent all of them in my university tuition of this year and also buying some useful textbooks.

I used to work at the restaurant as a part-time waitress and the small salary was insufficient for me to afford my life expense and more repayment at that time. Fortunately, I am so glad that I have been offered a new part-time job in an IT company recently where I can earn as double as before now, which means I am able to return more money to your bank every month. I am planning to repay 800 dollars each month and as a result the new contract length will be reduced to 6 months.
I hope that you can approve my new repayment application and look forward to your reply. Your faithfully,
Ken Hoang

To whom it may concern, During the fall of 2010, I successfully applied for a small business loan from the Greater National Bank. With the $100,000 I received, I was able to open a shop that creates custom shoes for the elderly. As part of the condition of the loan, my monthly payments were to be in instalments of $500.

Due to the ever changing global economy, my small shoe shop has become quite the popular online shopping experience. The yearly gross profits have increased by over %250 over the last 4 years. Now that the business has become highly profitable, I wish to increase the payment size of my business loan. I feel that a monthly payment of $1,000 is now financially feasible and responsible for the longevity of the business. I have calculated that if the profit margins continue at this pace, the business will be able to pay off the entirety of the loan by 2025.

Please contact me at your earliest convenience so that we may adjust the details of the loan. I look forward to our continued business and appreciate all the help that your bank has provided. Thank you for your time.
Sincerely,
Cherise Conway CEO, Grandma's Shoes

tasks.title: Responding to Survey Questions
scenario: Your manager is surveying your opinion about a scent-free workplace where perfumes and strong smells are not allowed. Many other workplaces in the city already have this policy.
tasks.instruction: Choose the option that you prefer. Why do you prefer your choice? Explain the reasons for your choice. Write about 150-200 words.
options: Option A: The workplace should have a scent-free policy.
Option B: The workplace should allow people to wear scents.

paragraphs: Hello Sir/Madam,
I strongly disagree to let people to wear or put a scent at our workplace, however I am also kind of not agree with other policy a scent -free policy because people still could put a scent.
In my opinion all the workplaces should not allowed people to wear perfumes or any other strong smells as many other workplaces in the city already decided.
Why I am choosing the first option due to the following points:

First, most of the workers in our place they do not like strong smells as I know Secondly, I watched last weekend on the television a pregame which was talking about the risks and illness in the workplaces. I have found a lot of illness vou could get because if smelling a strong perfumes.
To be honest, I have got an illness once from smelled a strong scent.
Finally, thank you to giving my a chance to give my opinion to the really important topic in the life.
All the best,
Al Hassan

Scent-free working policy is a debatable issue in different companies around Canada. In my opinion, this policy should be applied by all companies in the country. Every one of us would like to have a good smell all the time. However, this good smell might negatively affect the health of other people. As an example, a friend of mine is too sensitive to the strong smells and perfumes and his doctor told him to avoid them. Many other people are such as my friend and we should all respect this special need for them since our freedom ends when it hurts others.

In our daily work, we can not limit the people that we will meet everyday, so it is really hard to know if anyone will be negatively affected by the smell of your perfume. Applying a scent-free policy by our company will not insult any employee in the company but it will protect some people who are sensitive to such smells.
Hello Phil,

I have recently become aware that our workplace is considering adopting a scent-free environment policy. I strongly support this policy change. I believe that the other businesses in this city who have already adopted this policy are setting the standard for how the workplace environment should be.

I am of the opinion that people should be free to do whatever they wish so long as their actions do not harm others. There are various groups of people who are extremely sensitive to strong scents and can often suffer from serious health issues after exposure. For some people, strong scents like perfumes or colognes can trigger severe migraine headaches and can sometimes induce temporary blindness. For others, strong smells can trigger respiratory distresses like an asthmatic attack. By allowing workers to wear strong scents in the workplace, the company would be promoting an environment that compromises the health and safety of workers who are susceptible to these smells.
Thank you for giving me the opportunity to voice my opinion on this matter. Best regards,
Levla
